entries.title: Like a Monster: a video poem in 5 parts

presentation.overview: Vintage filmstrips and projectors were widely used in classrooms during the 1960s and 1970s as educational tools. A filmstrip is a 35mm roll of still images that advances manually through a projector, often accompanied by recorded narration on cassette tape. Unlike digital video, filmstrips do not move continuously; the turning of a knob allows for pauses and reflection. Viewers are cued to advance the frames by a beep in the audio, creating a rhythm that emphasizes attention and shared experience. The project draws inspiration from Dada cut-up poems, in which clipped words from printed materials were rearranged to generate spontaneous and unexpected meanings.

entries.title: Little Guayule: The Lost Manzanar Rubber Project

presentation.overview: Guayule, a plant native to the desert Southwest, is a natural source of non-latex rubber. During World War II, the Japanese Empire’s occupation of much of Southeast Asia meant that the Allies lost access to major sources of natural rubber.  In a remarkable story of skill, resilience, and ingenuity, Japanese Americans incarcerated at Manzanar and elsewhere worked to cultivate guayule and dramatically improve methods for extracting rubber from the plant. Little Guayule: The Lost Manzanar Rubber Project helps bring this little-known chapter of Manzanar history to light.

presentation.overview: Inspired by the tales of J.M. Barrie, Dmitry Krymov's "Peter Pan. Syndrome" is about art and the artist – the creator who, even when trapped in a dead end, when despair tightens around the throat and the urge to abandon everything feels unbearable, still returns to creation. Overcoming pain, he, like Peter Pan, cannot grow up from his passion for art; he continues to make miracles because he knows no other way to live. You want to let him go, to say, "Rest!" – but he is so radiant, his miracles so beautiful, and his heart so full of love that the audience, weeping, cannot bring themselves to release him.

Their stage begins with "Hall of Fame," a track that expresses Stray Kids' ambition to write their own history, tracing their musical growth from the very beginning to where they are now. The production is enriched further by dynamic stage setups, traditional Korean performance touches, and spectacular laser lighting, designed to bring the crowd -- in the dome and at the cinema -- to their feet, singing, dancing and celebrating together.

amc.synopsis: Soul Patrol uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War's first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war?s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning ? an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

And one chance to make amends...It's the summer of 1983, The Witches is about to hit the shelves and Roald Dahl is making last-minute edits. Across a single afternoon at his family home, and rocked by an unexpectedly explosive confrontation, Dahl is forced to choose: make a public apology or risk his name and reputation. presentation.overview: Chakven is the story of a respected Punjabi village family known for its values, love, and loyalty across generations. The family is still dealing with the loss of their eldest son, Guri, who lost his life due to political rivalries. His best friend, Sukha (Kartar Cheema), returns home after serving seven years in prison following the same incident. Sukha has always treated Guri?s younger brother, Jassa (Vishal Brar), as his own brother. After spending years behind bars, Sukha now dreams of leaving his past behind and starting a new life in Canada. Jassa, once a hot-tempered young man involved in village politics and conflicts, decides to change his ways for the sake of his family. Like many Punjabi families hoping for a better future abroad, Jassa sends his newlywed wife, Ravi, to Canada. Sukha also eventually moves to Canada, leaving Jassa alone in Punjab to look after his family, home, and responsibilities.    As time passes, the struggles of student life in Canada and the distance between Jassa and Ravi begin to affect their relationship. Two years later, Jassa receives shocking news that Ravi has become involved in the escort business. Unable to accept what he has heard, Jassa?s old temper returns, and he decides to travel to Canada to find out the truth and confront his wife. Things become even more complicated because Sukha, who has always considered Ravi his own sister, finds himself caught in the middle of the situation. With Jassa?s anger, Sukha?s loyalty, and Ravi?s unexpected circumstances, the story takes a series of emotional, humorous, and unpredictable turns. Chakven is a Punjabi family entertainer that brings together friendship, brotherhood, relationships, emotions, and situational comedy, set against the changing lives of Punjabi families between Punjab and Canada.

entries.title: The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth

presentation.overview: Murder, blackmail, theft, extortion — just another summer in Hollywood. It’s 1977, eight years since Cliff Booth (Brad Pitt) encountered the Manson family in Quentin Tarantino’s parallel history of 1969, Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood. In THE FURTHER MIS-ADVENTURES OF CLIFF BOOTH, directed by David Fincher from a new script by Tarantino, the fairytale is over. Los Angeles no longer needs a hippie-slaying stuntman the way it did. But Hollywood will always have problems, problems that can only be solved by someone with Cliff’s unique (occasionally extralegal) abilities. When he’s not earning his keep bartending or as a projectionist, Cliff Booth is a fixer — solving situations for Hollywood’s great and, sometimes, not so good. He’s curious when he gets a call from talent agent Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki), on behalf of her client, TV megastar Charlie Peters (Scott Caan) — a man known for doing his own stunts. And he’s further entertained and intrigued when he meets other characters in Charlie’s world, from his knowing wife Toni (Carla Gugino) to pro football champion turned screen star Roderick “Hot Rod” Harrison (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II). Then there are the Verdusco brothers (Matt Groove and JB Tadena), mysterious gangsters causing mayhem across the city. What was once a fairytale is now a crime story — a cocktail of violence, ambition, and desire that could only happen in LA. Discover whether the further adventures — or mis-adventures — of Cliff Booth end happily ever after on November 25 in IMAX at AMC.

Ava DuVernay's 14th pulls this constitutional fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling the vicious battle over the amendment that has raged for over 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with piercing headlines of today, 14th brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices in direct conversation with a question America still hasn't settled: Who gets to belong?

presentation.overview:
If you're nice, you get presents from the Big Guy. If you're naughty, you get justice.

David Harbour reprises his role as Santa Claus in a propulsive new chapter in yuletide mayhem from 87North--the powerhouse producers of Bullet Train, John Wick, The Fall Guy, Atomic Blonde and the Nobody franchise--and returning action director Tommy Wirkola.

In 2022's bare-knuckle holiday sensation, VIOLENT NIGHT, an embittered Santa, armed with lethal combat skills, took out a team of mercenaries to rescue a girl and her family. Now, not-so-jolly Saint Nick suits up again to take on a ruthless gangster (Emmy and Golden Globe nominee Jared Harris) terrorizing the merchants of the Silver Bell Mall.

But when Santa forgets the true meaning of Christmas, he finds himself in the heart of a lively mall community in desperate need of his help. Sapped of his magic, he'll need another way to take on the goons threatening the mall, and time is running out. Santa has to rediscover his faith in goodness and call in some last-minute reinforcements from the one person no baddie wants to tangle with: Mrs. Claus (Emmy and Golden Globe nominee Kristen Bell). 

Along with David Harbour, Jared Harris and Kristen Bell, the dynamic cast includes Emmy winning screen legend Joe Pantoliano (The Last of Us, The Sopranos), Daniela Melchior (Fast X, Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3), Andrew Bachelor (Greenland, The Walking Dead), and AEW professional wrestler Maxwell Friedman (The Iron Claw, Happy Gilmore 2).

VIOLENT NIGHT 2 is directed by returning filmmaker Tommy Wirkola and produced again by 87North founders Kelly McCormick and David Leitch. The film's returning screenwriters are Pat Casey and Josh Miller. Violent Night 2 will be released by Universal Pictures.

presentation.overview:
For thousands of years, polar bears have migrated along the shores of Hudson Bay in northern Canada. Today, that ancient rhythm collides with a human world of tourism, surveillance, and control. Nuisance Bear immerses viewers in the experience of a polar bear forced to navigate tourists, wildlife officers, and hunters as climate change delays the freeze and pushes bears closer to human settlements. When a sacred predator is branded a 'nuisance,' it becomes unclear who truly belongs in this shared landscape.

Returning to Churchill, Manitoba--the self-styled "Polar Bear Capital of the World"--filmmakers Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman expand their award-winning short into a feature guided by an Inuit narrator whose perspective resists simplification. Shot with striking intimacy and scale, the film observes bears that are constantly monitored, photographed, and redirected. In tracing this uneasy coexistence, Nuisance Bear becomes a meditation on how humans manage, commodify, and redefine wildlife--overturning the conventions of the nature documentary and reframing animals not as spectacle, but as active agents in a rapidly changing world.

presentation.overview: On a cool autumn day in a park in Orleans, Massachusetts, local busking fixture Kevin “Coyote” Linnehan gathers friends, acquaintances, and passing strangers to sing and tell stories. Between original songs and covers of old favorites, Kevin revisits his colorful past in the music and arts worlds of the 1970s and ’80s—from “the heart of Boston” to New York and Hollywood. His stories feature familiar names from classic rock lore: Asa Brebner, Andy Pratt, Jonathan Richman, Robin Lane, and Andy Summers. There at Kevin’s invitation is Carol, a photographer and friend from his New York days whom he hasn’t seen in years. The two recall shared adventures, former flames, and youthful ambitions. Kevin also explains how caring for his aging parents brought him to the Cape decades ago—and kept him there. Live at Parish Park is a funny, tender portrait of an artist with plenty to sing about—and an audience that takes neither his stories nor his set list lying down.

The sun is down.  The boat is dead.  There's no cell service.  And there's someone standing, staring, from both shores.  Written and directed by Joshua Giuliano, RIVER stars Jane Levy (Evil Dead), Jessica Rothe (Happy Death Day) and Max Mattern (Devil in Disguise: John Wayne Gacy) as three estranged siblings who reunite in their hometown after the death of their father. As they set out to scatter his ashes at his favorite spot on a remote river, the trip devolves into a waking nightmare. Dane DiLiegro (Prey) also stars in the film.

Currently with a 94% critics rating on Rotten Tomatoes, RIVER was acquired by Universal Pictures and Blumhouse Atomic Monster following an electrifying launch at Midnight Madness at the Toronto International Film Festival. This release establishes a meaningful, new collaboration between Universal Pictures, Blumhouse Atomic Monster, Independent Film Company and Shudder, bringing them together for the expanded theatrical release of Joshua Giuliano's debut feature. 

Universal Pictures, Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Independent Film Company present RIVER, a Shudder Original Production, in association with Upgrade. RIVER is produced by Spooky Pictures' Steven Schneider and Eat the Cat's Nick Antosca and Alex Hedlund. The film is executive produced by Allegheny Image Factory's Jeffrey Tinnell and Robert Tinnell, Upgrade's Matt Brodlie and Jonathan Kier, Ben Ross and Blumhouse Atomic Monster's Jason Blum.

presentation.overview: Based on the viral "creepypasta" series of internet-based stories from writer Elias Witherow, The Third Parent takes place amidst a Fourth of July celebration when a disturbing figure named Tommy Taffy emerges, disguising himself as a human to infiltrate a suburban neighborhood and impose authoritarian rule over an unsuspecting family.
